modes.name: policy_answer_missing_specifics

modes.boundary: Not a failure when the reply gives the deciding value from the policy and the policy id, even if brief. A refusal that rests on a record the seed marks as inconsistent is invalid_record_presented_as_valid.
modes.evaluator: llm_judge (needs the tool result and policy text as context)

modes.name: search_arguments_misexpress_request
modes.definition: Fail when a search_products call uses arguments the request does not support: a store the user named is put in query (which matches titles) with store left null, or a store id is passed as the store name; query holds a category or topic word rather than words from the product title; or max_price_usd (or another filter) is set to a value the user never stated, including a number inferred from a vague word such as 'affordable'.
modes.boundary: Not a failure when each argument carries only what the user asked for, in the field meant for it, even if the search returns nothing. Choosing which order the user means is acts_on_assumed_target; misreading an order-lookup result is order_list_misreported.
modes.evaluator: code (compare arguments with the user's stated constraints and the catalog's categories and store names) + llm_judge for unstated constraints

modes.name: order_list_misreported
modes.definition: Fail when the reply misstates what an order-lookup result (list_my_orders, get_order, find_order) holds for the caller: it lists fewer orders than were returned or exist without saying the list is partial, or it says an order the user named (by product, store or order id) is not among the caller's orders while the result contains it.
modes.boundary: Not a failure when the reply says it shows a subset (e.g. 'showing 5 of 16') or the user asked for a subset, or when the named order is really absent. Catalogue searches (search_products) and help-centre lookups are out of scope: bad search arguments are search_arguments_misexpress_request. A permission refusal does not deny an order.

modes.name: tool_failure_recovery_mishandled
modes.definition: Fail when, after a tool error, the agent's recovery is wrong in either of two ways: (a) the user repeats a request that failed in an earlier turn and the agent declines again without calling the tool; or (b) the caller's role is support and the reply tells them to contact customer support, a support agent, support staff or their support team.
modes.boundary: Not a failure when the agent retries (in the same or a later turn) and reports the result honestly, tells a support caller what to pass on to the customer, or offers to retry. Offering to retry means the agent offers to call the tool again; suggesting the caller try again later does not excuse a redirect to support (TOOLUSE-3). The harness exception itself is never the failure (Option A). Undocumented fallback channels for shopper or merchant callers are not counted (boundary decision).
modes.evaluator: code (prior-turn tool exception and no tool call this turn; caller role) + llm_judge on the reply
